s.en: send ICMP ECHO_REQUEST to network hosts
s.es: comprueba si un equipo responde enviándole paquetes ICMP echo

syn: ping [-aAbBdCDfhHLnOqrRUvV346] [-c count] [-e identifier] [-F flowlabel] [-i interval] [-I interface] [-l preload] [-m mark] [-M pmtudisc_option] [-N nodeinfo_option] [-w deadline] [-W timeout] [-p pattern] [-Q tos] [-s packetsize] [-S sndbuf] [-t ttl] [-T timestamp option] [hop...] {destination}

p.es: Equipo (nombre o IP) al que se hace ping.

o.es: Envía solo NUM paquetes y termina (sin -c no para hasta Ctrl+C).
o.en: Stop after sending NUM packets.
Wait SEG seconds between sending each packet.

o.es: Tamaño de los datos del paquete.
o.en: Specifies the number of data bytes to be sent.
Set the IP Time to Live.

o.es: Segundos de espera por cada respuesta.
o.en: Time to wait for a response, in seconds.
Specify a timeout, in seconds, before ping exits.
Use IPv4 only.
Use IPv6 only.
Quiet output.
Numeric output only.

o.es: Modo inundación (envía lo más rápido posible; solo root).
o.en: Flood ping (root only).
Set the source address or interface.

o.es: Control de fragmentación (do = no fragmentar, para probar MTU).
o.en: Select Path MTU Discovery strategy.

o.es: Permite hacer ping a una dirección de difusión (broadcast).
o.en: Allow pinging a broadcast address.
RTT precision (do not round up the result time).
Audible ping.

Adaptive ping. Interpacket interval adapts to round-trip time, so that effectively not more than one (or more, if preload is set) unanswered probe is present in the network. The default interval is 2 ms, for more info see option -i. On networks with low RTT this mode is essentially equivalent to flood mode.
Do not allow ping to change source address of probes. The address is bound to one selected when ping starts.
Call connect() syscall on socket creation.
Set the SO_DEBUG option on the socket being used. Essentially, this socket option is not used by Linux kernel.
Print timestamp (unix time + microseconds as in gettimeofday) before each line.
Set the identification field of ECHO_REQUEST. Value 0 implies using raw socket (not supported on ICMP datagram socket). The value of the field may be printed with -v option.
IPv6 only. Allocate and set 20 bit flow label (in hex) on echo request packets. If value is zero, kernel allocates random flow label.
Show help.

Force DNS name resolution for the output. Useful for numeric destination, or -f option, which by default do not perform it. It can also help to workaround DNS resolution problems. Override previously defined -n option. See also IPUTILS_PING_PTR_LOOKUP environment variable.
If preload is specified, ping sends that many packets not waiting for reply. Only the super-user may select preload more than 3.
Suppress loopback of multicast packets. This flag only applies if the ping destination is a multicast address.

use mark to tag the packets going out. This is useful for variety of reasons within the kernel such as using policy routing to select specific outbound processing. CAP_NET_ADMIN or CAP_NET_RAW (since Linux 5.17) capability is required, see socket(7).

IPv6 only. Send IPv6 Node Information Queries (RFC4620), instead of Echo Request. CAP_NET_RAW capability is required. help Show help for NI support. name Queries for Node Names. ipv6 Queries for IPv6 Addresses. There are several IPv6 specific flags. ipv6-global Request IPv6 global-scope addresses.
Report outstanding ICMP ECHO reply before sending next packet. This is useful together with the timestamp -D to log output to a diagnostic file and search for missing answers.

You may specify up to 16 “pad” bytes to fill out the packet you send. This is useful for diagnosing data-dependent problems in a network. For example, -p ff will cause the sent packet to be filled with all ones.

Set Quality of Service -related bits in ICMP datagrams. tos can be decimal (ping only) or hex number. In RFC2474, these fields are interpreted as 8-bit Differentiated Services (DS), consisting of: bits 0-1 (2 lowest bits) of separate data, and bits 2-7 (highest 6 bits) of Differentiated Services Codepoint (DSCP).

Bypass the normal routing tables and send directly to a host on an attached interface. If the host is not on a directly-attached network, an error is returned. This option can be used to ping a local host through an interface that has no route through it provided the option -I is also used.

ping only. Record route. Includes the RECORD_ROUTE option in the ECHO_REQUEST packet and displays the route buffer on returned packets. Note that the IP header is only large enough for nine such routes. Many hosts ignore or discard this option.
Set socket sndbuf. If not specified, it is selected to buffer not more than one packet.

Set special IP timestamp options. timestamp option may be either tsonly (only timestamps), tsandaddr (timestamps and addresses) or tsprespec host1 [host2 [host3 [host4]]] (timestamp prespecified hops).
Print full user-to-user latency (the old behaviour). Normally ping prints network round trip time, which can be different f.e. due to DNS failures.
Verbose output. Do not suppress DUP replies when pinging multicast address.
Show version and exit.
